book_intro:
Blue Letter Bible bakanlığı ve BLB Enstitüsü, Kutsal Yazıların tahrif edilemezliğine olan kesin inancı içeren tarihsel, muhafazakar Hristiyan inancına bağlıdır. BLB tarafından sağlanan metin ve ses içeriği çeşitli Evanjelik gelenekleri temsil ettiğinden, kaynak materyallerde aktarılan tüm fikir ve ilkelerin bu bakanlık tarafından toplamda onaylanması gerekmez.

Blue Letter Kutsal Kitap çalışma araçları Kutsal Kitap'ı okumayı, araştırmayı ve çalışmayı kolay ve ödüllendirici hale getirir.

notes.text: From 2 Sam. 5:1–3, omitting the war with Ishbosheth and David’s seven-year reign in Hebron as king (2 Sam. 2:1–4:12; 5:4–5; contrast 1 Chron. 3:4; 29:27). according to the word of the Lord by Samuel. See 1 Sam. 13:14; 15:28.
your bone and flesh. Despite a distinct division between Judah and the rest of Israel, they still recognized each other as family (compare “brothers”; 2 Sam. 2:26–27).

From 2 Sam. 5:6–10. The conquest of Jerusalem by David and all Israel (see 2 Sam. 5:6, “the king and his men”) gave the tribes a focus for their national unity. Thinking of his fellow Israelites living after the exile, the Chronicler presents Jerusalem as the possession not just of Judah but of “all Israel.”
the Millo. See note on 2 Sam. 5:9.
From 2 Sam. 23:8–39, with additional material (1 Chron. 11:41b–47). These details of David’s mighty men illustrate the support David received from the people around him and from God (v. 10).

The Chronicler may have intentionally skipped over material about Shammah from 2 Sam. 23:9–11. In that case the plurals “they . . . their” in 1 Chron. 11:14 (see esv footnote) indicate that others (possibly including David) were with Eleazar in this battle at Pas-dammim. This location was not mentioned in 2 Samuel.
The identity of these three mighty men is not known.
He poured it out to the Lord. See note on 2 Sam. 23:16–17.
The original list of the thirty (vv. 26–40b = 2 Sam. 23:24–39) has been supplemented with material from a different source (1 Chron. 11:41b–47; see note on 2 Sam. 23:8–39).
